Hi Sandra / Mike — thanks again for the 45-min call today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we stay aligned. I’ve attached a first-pass "Buying Passport" (spreadsheets) that codifies stakeholders, decision criteria, and an initial mutual action plan (MAP).

Call highlights:
- Primary use case: accelerate claims-processing automation for downstream provider payments; expected ~1000 weekly transactions during POC.
- Economic buyer: Sandra Lee (VP Ops) — priority: predictable cost per inference and SLA for 95th pct latency.
- Security/legal: Tina Marshall (Legal) + internal security team — focus on SOC 2, data residency, and encrypted in-transit & at-rest keys.
- Procurement: Mike Torres — timeline preference: PO for paid POC by end of September if POC performance hits targets.

Initial decision criteria (as discussed):
1) Latency at 95th pct <= 300ms per request for 512-token average.
2) Monthly unit cost under $X/token (TBD in pricing exercise).
3) SOC 2 Type II evidence and support for customer-managed KMS.
4) Ability to run a 2-week production-flavored POC with synthetic traffic and one real integration skeleton.

Proposed immediate next steps:
- Action 1 (Owner: Redwood / Jasmine): Share Buying Passport v0.1 with stakeholder ledger and a first-pass MAP (attached).
- Action 2 (Owner: QuantumHealth / Sandra): Confirm legal and security contacts + any data residency constraints by EOD Fri 24 Aug.
- Action 3 (Owner: Procurement / Mike): Confirm preferred PO timing and any standard contract clauses that might impact SOW.
- Action 4 (Owner: Redwood / Ben): Draft a concise POC plan (3 deliverables + success criteria) for review by Mon 27 Aug.

Attachments: QH_BuyingPassport_v0.1.xlsx (stakeholders + timeline).

If this looks right, I’ll fold feedback into MAP v1 and route a short one-pager SOW + target pricing for the procurement queue.

Thanks — Jasmine
